title: Find Nearest Point That Has the Same X or Y Coordinate
summary: Given a current location (x, y) and an array of points, find the index of the nearest valid point that shares an x or y coordinate with the current location.
statement: Given a current location (x, y) and an array of points, find the index of the nearest valid point that shares an x or y coordinate with the current location. If multiple points are equally close, choose the one with the smallest index. If no valid points exist, return -1. The Manhattan distance between two points is the sum of the absolute differences of their coordinates.
constraints: A point is valid when its x-coordinate equals x or its y-coordinate equals y.
Return the valid point with minimum Manhattan distance, breaking ties by smaller input index; return -1 if none.
hints: Only axis-aligned candidates need distance comparison.
Scan points in input order and update only on a strictly smaller valid distance.
Track the best Manhattan distance and its index, leaving ties unchanged.
Filtering enforces validity, strict improvement preserves the first tied index, and scanning covers every candidate.
editorial: Filtering enforces validity, strict improvement preserves the first tied index, and scanning covers every candidate.

tests.explanation: Valid indices one, two, and four have distances three, one, and one, so smaller tied index two wins.
The only point shares neither coordinate, so return -1.
